subject: A93782333D92EAE03CD81416F31AA617
introduction: On the evening of 22 May 1844, in an upper room in Shiraz, a young merchant told a visiting seeker that he was the Báb, the Gate. The Bahá’í era is dated from that night; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, who was born on it, kept the anniversary. This guide gathers Nabíl’s account of the conversation, the Báb’s own words about what had come upon Him, explanations of the title, and Tablets for the day. Nearly every part has a Gospel counterpart: “I am the door”; the first disciple finding his brother; hearts burning on the road to Emmaus; a forerunner who “was not that Light”; and the objection from scripture, “Shall Christ come out of Galilee?”
questions: The Báb’s claim was first made to one person, privately. What does that suggest about how a religion begins?
What did the title “Gate” mean to those who first heard it, and what did it come to mean?
People rejected Jesus by quoting prophecy. What would it take to read prophecy differently?

outside.why: Mullá Ḥusayn seated in the presence of the Báb, at night. Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?
“The Spirit of God had permeated and taken possession of My soul.” Isaiah’s call: mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts.
“I am the Báb, the Gate of God.” I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.
“O thou who art the first to believe in Me!” Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, we have found the Messias.
At a young age, in His twenty-fifth year. At twelve: wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?
What He intended by the term Gate. Of another forerunner: he was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.
The Tree of Sinai has spoken. God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses.
“I was born the night the Báb declared.” The dayspring from on high hath visited us, to give light to them that sit in darkness.
The year 1260 marked the first appearance. When the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son.
The anniversary, a blessed day. This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
The Night from whose day the Morn of Eternity dawned. Arise, shine; for thy light is come.
The Primal Point appeared. Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple.
He gave glad tidings of My manifestation. I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord.
Recognition by one traveller in an upper room. Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee. What makes one person recognize what a city of scholars misses?

A claim proved from the Text. The objection in every age is also from the text: shall Christ come out of Galilee? Hath not the scripture said, out of Bethlehem? How do the readings expect prophecy to be read?
